_comment: Source of /corrections/ (scripts/lib/discovery.mjs renderCorrectionsMain). Every retired public claim stays listed: add entries, never drop them. Each entry is Was / Now / Why, one line each, within the word budget in docs/messaging-canon.md, with the date retired. Strings may carry [text](href) links and nothing else.
description: Public claims Lupine Science has retired, each with the date and the reason: what we said, what we say now, and why.
intro: When we retire a public claim, we list it here with the date and the reason; what we claim now is on the [results page](/results/), and older wording stays in our public git history.

entries.title: “Verified AI predictions”
entries.was: “Verified AI predictions for materials discovery”; “the trust layer” as what we offer.
entries.now: We measure where machine-learned models of atoms go wrong and publish every verdict, failures included.
entries.why: Our evidence supports measurement, not verification. In Round 4 (July 2026) no gate passed.

entries.title: Runtime correction as a product
entries.was: “corrects that error at runtime as a physical field beside the model”.
entries.now: Correction is a research question here, not a product: it has held only in narrow, stated cases.
entries.why: The one correction that held blind covers one model, two metals, one facet; both Round-4 correction tests failed.

entries.title: “~70% of dominant error directions are shared”
entries.was: “~70% of dominant error directions are shared”; “errors span only 1.1–2.0 directions”.
entries.now: Retired as evidence. In our machine-learned benchmark, apparent cross-model alignment sat inside a coupling-aware null.
entries.why: It was a mean cosine over four classical (EAM) potentials, shown as if it described machine-learned ones.

entries.title: Theorem counts as evidence
entries.was: “899 build-locked theorems in the open Lean library, zero sorry” as a headline.
entries.now: Lean 4 checks the arithmetic and stated inequalities behind published numbers; it does not check the physics, the reference data or the pipeline.
entries.why: A count of checked statements says nothing about whether the physics is right.

entries.title: “17.84 → 9.92 GPa” and a usable class-aware correction
entries.was: Elastic error “17.84 → 9.92 GPa” and “zero no-harm violations”, presented as a usable correction.
entries.now: A ceiling, not a deployable correction: it needs the held-out answer to set its size. See [results](/results/#elastic-ceiling-16).
entries.why: 9.92 GPa was an in-sample recalibration. Neither figure is a correction you could apply to a new material.

entries.title: “5–12 GtCO₂/yr” as a Lupine outcome
entries.was: “Five Materials for 5–12 GtCO₂/Year”, as a climate outcome our work would unlock.
entries.now: Climate materials are one lane of where the work is aimed (Direction). Literature estimates appear only attributed to their sources.
entries.why: The range summed literature estimates. We have not measured or enabled any climate outcome.

entries.title: Organisations described as partners
entries.was: Labs, companies and agencies named as partners or pilots, with partner tiers and maps.
entries.now: We cite published work as sources, and welcome labs that want their models or materials measured.
entries.why: None of the organisations named were partners.

entries.title: Environmental-series capability claims
entries.was: One correction layer “fixes” water, air, PFAS, cement and refrigerant discovery; “corrected barriers recover DFT accuracy”; “certificates of synthesizability”.
entries.now: These pieces are marked Direction; each capability is a hypothesis to test.
entries.why: Our results contradict them: in Round 4 the barrier gate failed for every model, and both correction tests failed.

entries.title: “Proof pack”
entries.was: “Proof pack” for our evidence bundles, including a climate-series pack.
entries.now: “Evidence record”. The climate-series pack is retired; the shared DFT anchors record was reissued on November 12, 2026, reviewed internally (AI-assisted).
entries.why: The bundles check file integrity and provenance; they do not prove the claims inside them.

entries.title: The TMS2027 abstract’s universal “hyper-ribbon”
entries.was: The accepted poster abstract described a universal error “hyper-ribbon” that makes transferability predictable.
entries.now: A TMS2027 poster (Orlando, 14–18 March 2027), not a paper; the proceedings manuscript replaces it with narrower measurement claims.
entries.why: Registered stress tests did not support it, and a global elastic correction made results worse.

entries.title: 72.4% shown without its baseline
entries.was: “72.4% fewer DFT evaluations” with no baseline; booklet v1 called it “measured” and added ~38–76× multipliers.
entries.now: Projected, no new DFT, against four separate runs: only on the [shared DFT anchors](/articles/shared-dft-anchors/) page and booklet v1.1.
entries.why: Without its baseline a projection read as a saving. The undemonstrated multipliers were removed on November 12, 2026.

entries.title: “All four models under-predict every barrier”
entries.was: Round-4 and Z1 pages: every model under-predicted every barrier, 26 of 26 paths for one.
entries.now: Model-dependent at float64: CHGNet 25 of 28, MACE-MP-0 medium 21 of 29, small 17 of 26, MACE-MPA-0 medium 13 of 28 paths.
entries.why: That came from the float32 run; the locked float64 records show no universal direction.

entries.title: The investor one-pager and climate-investor presentation
entries.was: An investor one-pager at /one-pager and a climate-investor presentation.
entries.now: Removed; both addresses redirect to [company facts](/about/).
entries.why: Both were superseded drafts that repeated claims retired on this page.

entries.title: The funding status line
entries.was: A one-line funding status on the homepage, company facts, FAQ and llms.txt.
entries.now: No longer published. Research partners, model builders, press and investors can write to the address in [company facts](/about/#contact).
entries.why: We no longer publish a funding status.
